title: Mittens' Lost Bell
markdown:
Gertie the goblin had a ball! Not just any ball, mind you. It’s a super bouncy, fuzzy moss ball! Boing! Boing! it goes! And right beside her, purring like a little engine, is Mittens the cat. Mittens is sleek and black, and on her collar, there’s a tiny, shiny bell. When Mittens wiggles – and oh, she wiggles! – her bell goes ding-dong, ding-dong, like happy little raindrops.

The sunbeams were dancing on the rock where Mittens was napping. They looked like warm, golden ribbons, all soft and glowy. Ahhhh, it was such a peaceful afternoon. Sooooo peaceful.

But wait! Suddenly, Mittens sat up! Her green eyes, like shiny emeralds, popped wide open! She shook her head. Flick-flick. Then again! Shake-shake! But… where was the happy ding-dong? The special bell was gone!

“Oh nooo!” squeaked Gertie. Her eyebrows popped up so high, they nearly touched her little goblin hat! Mittens nudged her empty collar with her nose. A little sad “mrrrow” came out. Oh, her poor whiskers drooped just a little bit. This is sadness, Gertie thought, then quickly shook her head. “Don’t you worry, Mittens!” Gertie said, her voice warm and cozy like a hug. “We’ll find it! We always do! Remember when we played near the glowworm glade this morning? Maybe it fell off there!”

So then, hand-in-paw (well, a little goblin hand and a soft cat-paw!), they went on their super-important quest. The path was whispery, with the grass sighing secrets to the breeze. Shhhhh!

Soon, they were at the glowworm glade! It wasn't dark and spooky, oh no! Little glowworms, like teeny tiny fairy lights, blinked on and off all around them! They made soft, warm pools of light that danced on the leaves. It was like stepping into a sparkly dream! Gertie and Mittens tiptoed through the glow. Sniff, sniff. Mittens looked under a mushroom that was bigger than Gertie’s head! Gertie peeked behind dewdrops that sparkled like diamonds. But no bell. No happy ding-dong.

“Hmmm,” Gertie hummed, tapping her chin. “Where else did we play, Mittens?” Mittens remembered! She remembered peeking at the high rocks where Gribble the ogre lived. Gribble wasn't a scary ogre, oh no! He was the gentlest, biggest giant in the whole wide world! He loved making yummy things, like his famous wobbly puddings and bubbly soups.

As they got closer, a wonderful smell tickled their noses! It smelled warm and berry-sweet, and a little bit like… giggling sugar! And there he was! Gribble! He was standing by a huge, jiggly, wobbly pudding that quivered like a happy jelly! He wore a super clean apron, but there was a little smudge of purple berry juice right on the tip of his round, friendly nose. He was stirring the pudding with a spoon as big as Gertie!

“Hello, Gribble!” Gertie called, her voice bright and cheerful. Mittens gave a little, hopeful “mrrrow?”

Gribble looked up, his big eyes crinkling. “Oh, hello there, Gertie! And Mittens, my little furry friend! What a surprise!” His voice rumbled, like friendly thunder, but warm. “What brings you to my wobbly pudding world today?”

“Mittens lost her special bell,” Gertie explained, pointing to the empty collar. “The one that goes ding-dong. We think it might have fallen off when we were playing near here.”

Gribble put down his giant spoon with a soft thump. “A lost bell? Oh dear! That simply won’t do!” he rumbled. He looked down at his big feet, then around him. “I was just sweeping up a little bit of spilled snowberry dust and flour,” he said. “But sometimes things get a little jumbled when I'm making wobbly puddings. Perhaps… oh my goodness… could it be…?”

He reached into a big, smooth bowl filled with soft, fluffy, white flour. He rummaged gently. And then… clink-clank-ding-dong! Gribble pulled out Mittens’ silver bell! It had a little flour on it, but it was perfectly fine, shining in the light.

Mittens let out a happy little squeak, her tail doing a happy dance! She nudged the bell. Gertie giggled with relief. “You found it, Gribble! Thank you so much!”

Gribble beamed. “It's always best to be careful,” he said, and winked. “But sometimes, even careful cooks get a little jumbled! Especially with wobbly puddings around!” He carefully, ever so carefully, put the bell back onto Mittens’ collar.

Ding-dong! went the sweet little bell! Mittens purred with pure happiness, rubbing against Gribble’s big, flour-dusted leg.

Gertie and Mittens waved goodbye and headed home. The little bell sang its happy, tinkling tune as Mittens trotted beside Gertie. The sun was dipping low, painting the sky in soft pinks and oranges. They were safe and sound, and Mittens’ bell jingled merrily. Gertie knew that even a tiny adventure, shared with a good friend and a kind ogre, made the whole world feel even more wonderful and safe.

And so, Gertie and Mittens learned that a lost treasure, even a tiny one, can always be found with a little searching and a lot of kindness. And they also discovered that sometimes, the sweetest surprises are hidden in the most delightfully wobbly places.
characters: Gertie the young goblin, a cat
